sources.institution: Service public de Wallonie portal / Institut Destrée / Segefa
sources.title: Tournai et le Tournaisis sous influence anglaise (1513–1519)
sources.finding: Historian-created historical map distinguishes city Tournai from surrounding Tournaisis administrative territory in 1513–19. May be starting point for larger outer influence envelope; not equivalent to proven English direct control over each parish.
sources.caveat: Page claims Westminster Commons representation, contradicted by C.S.L. Davies 1998. Map copyrighted to SEGEFA/Institut Destrée (2013), no permission to copy/trace onto public atlas. It labels 'influence anglaise' not complete directly enforced rule.

sources.author: Florian Mariage
sources.title: Bailli royal, seigneurs et communautés villageoises: Jeux et enjeux de pouvoir(s) en Tournaisis (du XIVe siècle à la fin du XVIe siècle)
sources.verified: university dissertation catalogue and abstract read; full PDF access restricted
sources.finding: The Tournaisis bailiwick, Tournai–Tournaisis–Mortagne–Saint-Amand, organized roughly sixty rural parishes since 1383. Royal bailiff, fief holders, village courts, municipal jurisdictions overlap, so Tudor rule requires individual administrative evidence.
sources.caveat: ~60 parishes describes long-period local judicial geography; cannot assert all 60 directly governed by Henry VIII during 1513–19.

sources.institution: Irish Historical Studies / Cambridge University Press
sources.author: David B. Quinn
sources.title: Anglo-Irish Local Government, 1485–1534
sources.verified: journal abstract and reference list read
sources.finding: Royal administration in Dublin could nominally govern entire Ireland but in practice authority waned in successive groups of territories; includes Ormond lands and Irish Exchequer Memoranda Rolls as original administrative records.
sources.caveat: Older scholarship 1939, some specific details tentative; compare to Ellis 2021 Pale and later Irish historiography.

sources.author: Guy Van Dievoet
sources.title: Les coutumes du Tournaisis: droit rural ou droit urbain?
sources.finding: 1523 Tournai urban customary law applied by seventeen villages and later drafts for rest of Tournaisis bailiwick; points to different rural jurisdictions which cannot be equated to occupied medieval city walls.
sources.caveat: 1523 and later legal situation is after 1519; contextual map and late continuities only, not proof England governed those exact villages in 1515.

sources.institution: National Library of Scotland digitized historical literature
sources.title: The Clan Donald volume, chapter XI: under James IV 1493–1519
sources.verified: table of contents and indexed snippets read; primary citations not checked
sources.finding: 1513 post-Flodden western Scottish isles saw further local rebellion, Sir Donald of Lochalsh claimed lordship and made 1515 submission; local governance should not be uniformly painted as Scottish Crown direct in entire archipelago.
sources.caveat: Outdated interpretive framework possible, treat as research lead to original Scottish royal records; no exact polygon.
